text: Byrne describes coding as an iterative process in which increased familiarity can change interpretations. The researcher should document coding iterations so changes to codes and prospective themes remain transparent and earlier analytic paths can be revisited. In the worked example, a spreadsheet placed data items in rows and successive coding iterations in columns; original transcripts were consulted again as familiarity grew. The author revised, merged, generalized, or discarded codes when later interpretation showed that an earlier label was too vague, too specific, or less useful. This spreadsheet is the author's example of an audit aid, not a required software or data structure. (Publisher PDF pp. 1400–1402.)
